source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 18 ноября ст. ст. — «Мч. Платона (302 или 306).»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The head line gives him «(; - 306)» and the body states the year of the beheading, so a `death` is proposed, the folder carrying no `dates`. The entry is plainly him: he lived at the end of the third century, came from Ancyra of Galatia in Asia Minor and was the brother of the martyr Antiochus; taken young by the idolaters for proclaiming his faith and brought before the governor Agrippinus, who saw the beauty of the young man and knew he had property and tried flattery first, then threats, then had him flogged without mercy and tortured with red-hot rods, and finally ordered his beheading in 306. The page records fragments of his relics at the monasteries of Mega Spileo of Kalavryta, the Life-giving Spring on Poros and the Phaneromene on Salamis. The Ἀπολυτίκιον names him with Romanos and is copied onto both; the Κοντάκιον names him alone and is taken; the Οἶκος and the Κάθισμα are not drafted. **The brother Antiochus is named in the life without a link**: the corpus holds folders of that name but none of them was identified with this man, and no `related` row is proposed for him. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.12.2025 (18. новембар ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Платон.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND A LARGE CONFLICT RECORDED: this book beheads him «око 266. год.» where the folder holds «302 or 306», an interval already widened to hold two other calendars' readings of the Diocletianic persecution. ABOUT 266 IS THIRTY-SIX TO FORTY YEARS EARLIER AND FALLS OUTSIDE IT ENTIRELY, so it is not a narrowing and not a widening but a third reading, and writing it in would make the folder claim an interval 266–306 that no source states. Nothing moved; the year is written into the life as the book's own and is a line for the author. No `related` row: the men the entry names are the governor Agrippinus and Plato the philosopher, and neither is a saint of this corpus. WHAT THE ENTRY ADDS: Ancyra of Galatia named as today's Ankara, a Christian by birth and upbringing, the open preaching against the worship of dead creatures, the two deaths and two lives answered to the governor, red-hot iron balls laid on his bared body and strips cut from his skin, the cry to torture him harder so that the inhumanity and the endurance should both be plain, THE EXCHANGE ABOUT HIS NAMESAKE — that he is no more like Plato the philosopher than in the name, one teaching the wisdom which is Christ's and the other that which is folly before God — and the eighteen days in prison without food or water, with the answer to the astonished guards that they are filled with meat and he with holy prayers, they gladdened by wine and he by Christ the true vine. Measured: no other folder in the corpus holds the form «Платон», so it folds with nothing.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — «Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Platon; al Sfântul Mucenic Roman diaconul», glas 4, a common of martyrs printed once for the two of them; the page's «nesctricăciunii» is its own reading and is copied as it stands

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received from Thee, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Thy strength they overthrew the tormentors, and broke the powerless presumption of the demons. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Δυὰς ἡ εὐκλεής, τῶν κλεινῶν Ἀθλοφόρων, ἐδόξασε λαμπρῶς, τὴν Ἁγίαν Τριάδα, ὁ Πλάτων ὁ ἔνδοξος, Ρωμανὸς τε ὁ ἔνθεος, ἐναθλήσαντες, καὶ τὸν ἐχθρὸν καθελόντες, ὅθεν πάντοτε, ὑπὲρ ἠμῶν δυσωπούσι, τὸν μόνον Φιλάνθρωπον.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α’. Χορὸς Ἀγγελικός — printed on both men's pages for 18 Νοεμβρίου, and it names them both, so it is copied onto both folders.

english.text: The glorious pair of the renowned prize-winners — Plato the illustrious and Romanos filled with God — gloriously glorified the Holy Trinity by their contest, and pulled the enemy down; and so they entreat for ever on our behalf the only Lover of mankind.

hymns.text: Ἡ ἁγία μνήμη σου, τὴν οἰκουμένην εὐφραίνει, συγκαλοῦσα ἅπαντας, ἐν τῷ πανσέπτῳ ναῷ σου, ἔνθα νῦν, μέτ' εὐφροσύνης συναθροισθέντες, ᾄσμασι, σὰς ἀριστείας Πλάτων ὑμνοῦμεν, καὶ ἐν πίστει ἐκβοῶμεν· Βαρβάρων ῥῦσαι τὴν πόλιν σου Ἅγιε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’. Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — on the page of «Άγιος Πλάτωνας», and it names him.

english.text: Your holy memory gladdens the whole world, calling all together into your most venerable church, where, gathered now in joy, we sing your feats of valour, Plato, and cry out in faith: deliver your city from the barbarians, O Saint.

hymns.text: Мученицы Твои, Господи,/ во страданиих своих венцы прияша нетленныя от Тебе, Бога нашего,/ имуще бо крепость Твою,/ мучителей низложиша,/ сокрушиша и демонов немощныя дерзости./ Тех молитвами// спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 18 ноября ст. ст. — «Тропарь мучеников Платона и Романа»

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from thee our God; for having thy strength they cast down the tormentors and shattered the feeble insolence of the demons also. By their prayers save our souls.

hymns.text: Святая твоя память вселенную веселит,/ созывающи верныя вся в пречестный храм твой,/ идеже ныне, радостию совокупльшеся,/ поем в песнех и светлостех./ Сего ради, Платоне, вопием ти:// языческаго нашествия избави град твой, святе.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 18 ноября ст. ст. — «Кондак мученика Платона»

english.text: Thy holy memory gladdens the whole world, calling all the faithful into thy most honoured temple, where now, gathered together in gladness, we sing in hymns and in splendour. Therefore, O Plato, we cry out to thee: deliver thy city from the invasion of the heathen, O holy one.

death.note: The interval is widened to hold both readings and neither is narrowed. days.pravoslavie.ru prints its own disjunction twice, in the line for 18 ноября ст. ст. — «(302 или 306)» — and at the close of its life page, «(+ 302 или 306)». saint.gr gave the 306 this folder held flat. Neither page gives a year of birth.
